task.description: Surfaced by the two-client test while fixing SP-44. Ticket numbers are counted per store, and a worktree has its own store (tracked state follows the branch, ADR 0009), so two agents on two branches both mint CO-1 with different task ids and different files of the same name. Nothing is lost silently - git reports an add/add conflict on merge - but the resolution is unspecified: keeping one side discards the other agent work, keeping both leaves two tickets sharing one key, and nothing tells you which. Needs a decision and then a mechanism: either a storypole verb that renumbers one side before/after merge, or keys that carry a discriminator when the store is branch-local. Related: SP-35 (the test that found it), SP-44 (the in-store overwrite, fixed), ADR 0009.
task.title: Two branches mint the same ticket key and merge as an add-add conflict

events.description:
Surfaced by the two-client test while fixing SP-44. Ticket numbers are counted per store, and a worktree has its own store (tracked state follows the branch, ADR 0009), so two agents on two branches both mint CO-1 with different task ids and different files of the same name. Nothing is lost silently - git reports an add/add conflict on merge - but the resolution is unspecified: keeping one side discards the other agent work, keeping both leaves two tickets sharing one key, and nothing tells you which. Needs a decision and then a mechanism: either a storypole verb that renumbers one side before/after merge, or keys that carry a discriminator when the store is branch-local. Related: SP-35 (the test that found it), SP-44 (the in-store overwrite, fixed), ADR 0009.

FIXED 2026-11-08 (commit bd6c144, branch feat/gb-347-shared-keys), under ADR 0009.

Ticket numbers now come from one counter per repository, kept in the git directory - the only place shared by
every checkout and never tracked, so no ignore rules and no migration of tracked files. Allocation takes
max(counter, index), so a repository whose history predates the counter continues from the numbers in use.

Proof: two worktrees resolve to one counter directory and take 1 then 2, where before both took 1. Four unit
tests cover the sequence, the migration from an index, per-prefix counters and lock cleanup.

The rejection alternative, recorded because it is tempting: derive keys from something globally unique (a uuid)
and assign human numbers later. It buys nothing here - the counter is already globally unique per repository
and keeps keys stable, which receipts, plans and commit messages depend on.

The decision that made this a five-line change instead of a redesign is ADR 0009: coordination state follows
the checkout. SP-39 now applies the same rule to claim leases, which is the remaining half.
